modes.cue_notes: Sit sideways close to the wall, then swing the legs up as you lower your back to the floor. Legs rest vertically against the wall, hips close to the baseboard. Arms rest comfortably at the sides or on the belly. A folded blanket under the hips elevates them slightly for a more restful inversion. Allow the hamstrings and lower back to release passively.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: A restorative mild inversion. Kidney and bladder meridians run along the back of the leg and spine. Promotes venous return and nervous system downregulation.

breathing_cues.entering: As you swing the legs up, exhale fully and allow the lower back to soften into the floor before finding stillness.
breathing_cues.holding: Notice how the breath becomes noticeably fuller — the diaphragm meets less compression in this mild inversion. Let the belly rise freely on each inhale and feel a wave of release down the backs of the legs on each exhale.
breathing_cues.exiting: On an exhale, gently slide the legs down the wall or bend the knees toward the chest before rolling to one side.

modifications.name: Blanket under hips
modifications.description: Place a folded blanket or bolster under the hips to elevate the pelvis and create a gentler inversion angle, improving lymphatic drainage and reducing hamstring tension.

modifications.name: Feet wide on wall
modifications.description: Allow feet to separate wider on the wall into a V-shape, reducing hamstring intensity and adding a gentle inner groin stretch.

modifications.name: Bent knees on wall
modifications.description: For students with very tight hamstrings, scoot the hips back from the wall so the knees can be slightly bent while the legs still rest on the wall.

modifications.name: Supported butterfly legs
modifications.description: Bring the soles of the feet together against the wall in a butterfly shape, combining the inversion with a gentle inner groin and hip opener. Use blocks under thighs for support.

emotional_release_potential.notes: The inversion and complete passivity invite a letting-go quality associated with kidney energy. Students may experience a subtle emotional softening as venous return and nervous system tone shift toward deep rest.
This pose is traditionally used in restorative sequences for burnout and adrenal fatigue. Emotional exhaustion associated with depletion of kidney jing may surface as tears or quiet emotion.
